extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, patent examiners, and law students studying interference proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing declaration, notice, issues, preliminary statements, testimony, amendment, and proof in patent interference proceedings before the Patent Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and exact statement of conflicting claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must secure from adverse parties an exact statement of their conflicting claims and give notice thereof to the applicants or patentee, directing the primary examiner to proceed to determine the question of priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever an examiner discovers conflicting claims the duty is to notify such applicants/patentees/caveators and, if necessary, require them to state their claims so that the nature and extent of antagonism are distinct and unmistakable. Parties must put claims in such condition that no further change will be required to precisely cover their respective rights; want of exactness is sufficient reason to require further amendment. Parties who fail to comply with the notice will be excluded from the interference (but without prejudice to other rights).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and form of notices of interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of the interference must disclose the name and residence of each contestant and attorney, the date of filing of the contestant's application (or date/number if a patentee), the ordinals of conflicting claims, and the invention claimed — clearly and concisely defining them in as many counts as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices and accompanying files are transmitted to the examiner of interferences, who reviews them for defects; defective notices are returned for amendment and, upon perfection, the interference is formally declared and notices sent to parties with an order to file preliminary statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duty to define subject-matter and issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must see that the subject-matter put in issue by the interference is properly defined and must direct that the issues represent what the parties actually claim, not what they might claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issues must point out the conflicting claims and contain a summary of the contested matter; hypothetical issues are not permitted. The primary examiner must decide whether claims interfere, looking to the language of the application alone in declaring an interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues must have the same meaning to all parties; construction conclusive
rubrics_metrics.description: An issue must have the same meaning as to all claimants; if susceptible of various meanings, adopt the one which sustains the interference and best agrees with the specifications; the Patent Office's construction of an issue is conclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple constructions exist, the one that sustains the interference and aligns best with claimants' specifications will be adopted. The construction placed upon an issue by the Patent Office is final for the interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which applications/patents to include in an issue
rubrics_metrics.description: The issues must embrace only those applications and patents which conflict with all the others; cross-interferences should be consolidated by presenting them in different counts of the same issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single interference can embrace only such applications/patents as conflict with all the others. When one application conflicts with two or more patents only one interference should be declared and all be made parties; related cross-interferences can be consolidated into counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to be a party to the interference
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant is not entitled to be a party to an interference unless his right against the public is complete: he must have performed an entire inventive act (conception and reduction to practice), produced a protectable art/instrument, possessing novelty and utility, and not abandoned to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each applicant stands on individual merits; if on his merits he could not lawfully receive a patent, he cannot be permitted to contest priority. Examiner passes on these questions as in ordinary ex parte applications with the same rights of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary statement required content
rubrics_metrics.description: The preliminary statement must be a concise sworn recital of the date of original conception, construction of a drawing or model, disclosure to others, reduction to practice, and extent of use; if made abroad, when/where patented or published and when introduced into the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The principal object is to fix relative times of inventive acts. The statement should embrace all facts the applicant intends to rely on (records or extrinsic testimony). It must be sealed before filing and is not to be opened until all parties' statements are filed or time expires and the examiner has inspected and found it satisfactory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusive nature of preliminary statement dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Dates given in the preliminary statement are considered conclusive on the claimant; subsequent evidence must confirm and not contradict them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The earliest dates fixed by a statement are conclusive against the claimant's future claims to an earlier date. 'On or about' a date is interpreted as that exact date, not an earlier one. Dates fixed by belief may sometimes be corrected by evidence; however, an amendment inserting an earlier date inconsistent with the proof is not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealing and limited inspection of preliminary statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary statements must be sealed up before filing and cannot be opened for examination by opposing parties until all are filed or the time for filing has expired and the examiner has inspected them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the integrity of each party's claimed dates while allowing the examiner to review. Either contestant may be required to correct defects within a specified period; original or amended statements cannot be returned once filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to file a preliminary statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file the preliminary statement within the prescribed time forfeits the party's right to be heard for an earlier inventive date than his application filing date; judgment goes against a later conflicting applicant at once on the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the later of several conflicting applicants fails to file, he ceases to be a party and the interference proceeds among the others. If none file, priority is awarded to the senior applicant. In re-issue cases the date of the original application is the prima facie date if the re-issue applicant does not file a preliminary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and limits for amending preliminary statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations in a preliminary statement are presumed correct and conclusive unless procured by fraud; amendments of substance are allowed only on motion showing the amendment is essential to justice and are constrained by timeliness and cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clerical errors may be corrected at any time if no injustice results. Material amendments should be made before testimony is taken and as soon as the error is discovered; ignorance of law or attorney neglect are not favored grounds, though Commissioner may permit amendment in proper cases. Amendments are barred where errors arose from negligence or where amendment would unfairly prejudice adversaries (laches). A party cannot file a defective statement, become familiar with the adversary's case, and then amend to his advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination and comparison of preliminary statements to applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing time has elapsed, the preliminary statements are examined and compared with the original applications; if a later applicant's claimed date does not anticipate the filing date of the earliest application, priority is awarded to the earliest applicant and judgment is entered against the later party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only where a party's preliminary statement anticipates the filing of an earlier application does the interference proceed further; otherwise the prima facie presumption arising from dates of filing suffices to award priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling and procedures for taking testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner fixes times for taking testimony: a period for the latest applicant's direct case, a period for the adverse party's reply, and a period for the later applicant's rebuttal; time for multiple contestants arranged so each can present and rebut evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions may be granted on motion showing under oath reasons for inability to obtain evidence, names of witnesses, facts expected to be proved, and prior efforts to secure attendance. Failure to complete testimony within assigned time does not automatically delay final hearing; hearing may be postponed for sufficient reasons but, absent postponement, a party who has completed evidence may insist on hearing and judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of evidence and burden/standard of proof for priority
rubrics_metrics.description: General rules of evidence apply; priority consists of prior conception plus reduction to practice or reasonable diligence in reducing to practice; successful claimant must establish priority by a clear preponderance of the evidence (not necessarily beyond reasonable doubt) and must overcome presumptions arising from earlier applications and patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claimant must establish his conception and reduction to practice and must affirmatively demonstrate right to priority as against adversaries (sufficient to defeat their patents in the courts). In an interference with a patent, the applicant must offer such evidence of priority as would defeat the patent in court. The examiner has exclusive authority to decide competency, construction, scope and legal meaning of foreign patents/other evidence when determining whether they cover the same invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to interference materials and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Adverse parties in an interference are allowed to see copies of interfering claims and specifications, but other persons cannot have access to interference files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interference files are not public; only the contestants (and their attorneys) may inspect the specific materials necessary for the contest.
